newsitem.title: ROMANIA: SOCCER-ROMANIAN REFEREE DENIES BRIBERY ALLEGATION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROMANIAN REFEREE DENIES BRIBERY ALLEGATION.

text.p: A Romanian ex-referee has denied allegations that he was approached to fix a European Cup Winners' Cup match between Porto and Aberdeen 12 years ago.
"I'm totally surprised about these allegations," said retired match official Ioan Igna on Thursday. "I don't know this person who is making accusations. I've never spoken to him."
Portuguese police questioned businessman Fernando Barata after he alleged that Porto had asked him to fix a 3-0 victory against the Scottish side.
Barata has said that he had been asked to speak to the Romanian referee ahead of the match. But he made no mention of how much money was offered.
Porto, who strongly denied the accusations, won both legs of the tie 1-0.
Igna said said Porto had provided all three Romanian officials for the match with air tickets, accommodation and food.
"They gave me a watch, a little flag and a badge for presents. Nothing else," he said.
"This is a war of words within the Portuguese media. It has nothing to do with me. I remember Porto was even angry at me after the match for not awarding a penalty."
